domain_entities.name: Employee
domain_entities.purpose: The authenticated actor and the subject of leave data. Gains a nullable credential (passwordHash) so a caller can authenticate; null means the employee has no login credential yet.

domain_entities.name: AuthToken
domain_entities.purpose: The bearer credential minted at login and verified by the auth hook. Its payload contract (sub = employee id, role = EmployeeRole) is fixed by the existing verifier and must not change.

domain_entities.name: LeaveRequest
domain_entities.purpose: The leave application being read. No lifecycle change in this feature; reads are status-unrestricted for visibility.

domain_entities.name: LeaveBalance
domain_entities.purpose: The caller's leave balance for one leave type and one accrual period. The read surface adds a computed `available` figure; OPEN vs CLOSED remains inferred from period bounds.

domain_entities.name: LeavePolicy
domain_entities.purpose: The effective policy governing a leave type's entitlement and accrual period. Balance reads enumerate policies (not the leave-type catalog) to derive which leave types have a current period.

business_rules: requestedDays = endDate - startDate + 1 (inclusive calendar days, whole-day UTC, no weekend/holiday exclusion) is the single canonical day-count derivation used everywhere a day count is needed. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever requestedDays / day-count derivation appears, not only here]

Date-range filtering is inclusive on both edges: startDateFrom <= startDate <= startDateTo and endDateFrom <= endDate <= endDateTo. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequestQueryParams date-range filtering appears, not only here]

Leave visibility is role-scoped: EMPLOYEE sees only their own requests; MANAGER sees their own plus direct reports (employee.managerId === actor.id), one level only, not transitive; ADMIN sees all. The same rule governs both list and single-request reads. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest visibility appears, not only here]

Manager visibility is status-unrestricted: a manager sees direct reports' requests in every status plus their own. Visibility and authority to act are separate; the existing decide authorization (SUBMITTED-only) is unchanged. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest visibility vs decide authority appears, not only here]

A caller who may not see a leave request receives the same response as one that does not exist (404), so the endpoint cannot be used to probe for ids. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest single-read authorization appears, not only here]

A wrong email and a wrong password are indistinguishable in the login response (same status, same message), so the endpoint cannot enumerate accounts. passwordHash is never returned in any response body. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever Login credential verification appears, not only here]

The accrual period containing a date is derived from the employee's hireDate, stepping accrualPeriodMonths at a time, using pure UTC date arithmetic (startOfUtcDay, addMonths, periodContaining). Exactly one shared implementation exists and is reused by both the leave and balance paths. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever Accrual-period derivation appears, not only here]

Balance enumeration iterates POLICIES, not the leave-type catalog. At most one policy per leaveTypeCode is selected: status ACTIVE, effectiveFrom <= asOf, and (effectiveTo IS NULL OR effectiveTo >= asOf); if more than one remains, take the latest effectiveFrom. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever Effective policy selection for balance reads appears, not only here]

When no balance row exists for a policy's current period, that leave type is omitted from the balance list (never synthesized). An employee with no open periods gets an empty list (valid 200), never an error. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever Balance list composition appears, not only here]
available = entitledDays - usedDays - pendingDays (computed, not persisted). [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveBalance.available appears, not only here]
The authenticated actor is always resolved from the verified token (request.user), never from a client-supplied id. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever Actor resolution appears, not only here]
domain_notes:
Domain slice for authentication + read endpoints (v3).

New/changed entities:
- Employee gains `passwordHash: string | null` (nullable credential; null = no login credential). Lifecycle unchanged: ACTIVE, TERMINATED, ON_LEAVE.
- AuthToken (new): payload contract fixed by the existing verifier — sub = employee id, role = EmployeeRole. Lifecycle: ISSUED, EXPIRED.
- LeaveRequest: unchanged shape (14 fields incl. cancelledBy/cancelledAt); lifecycle DRAFT, SUBMITTED, APPROVED, REJECTED, CANCELLED. This feature is read-only — no state transitions added.
- LeaveBalance: gains computed `available` (not persisted). Lifecycle OPEN, CLOSED (inferred from period bounds, unchanged).
- LeavePolicy: unchanged; lifecycle DRAFT, ACTIVE, SUPERSEDED. Balance reads enumerate policies (not the leave-type catalog) to derive current-period leave types.

Binding business rules (scope broad):
- requestedDays = endDate - startDate + 1 (inclusive calendar days, UTC) is the single canonical day-count derivation.
- Date-range filtering inclusive on both edges.
- Role-scoped leave visibility: EMPLOYEE self-only; MANAGER self + direct reports (managerId === actor.id, one level, non-transitive); ADMIN all. Same rule for list and single-read.
- Manager visibility is status-unrestricted; visibility and decide authority are separate (decide stays SUBMITTED-only).
- Unauthorized single-read returns the same 404 as a nonexistent id (no id probing).
- Login: wrong email vs wrong password indistinguishable; passwordHash never in any response.
- Accrual-period derivation shared (startOfUtcDay/addMonths/periodContaining, pure UTC, anchored on hireDate) — one implementation reused by leave and balance paths.
- Effective policy selection: at most one per leaveTypeCode (ACTIVE, effectiveFrom <= asOf, effectiveTo null or >= asOf; tie-break latest effectiveFrom).
- No balance row for a policy's current period → omit that leave type; no open periods → empty list (200), never an error.
- available = entitledDays - usedDays - pendingDays.
- Actor always resolved from the verified token, never a client-supplied id.

No open questions: all boundary/count/range semantics were settled by the feature's binding decisions.
